questions: Should datetime objects be serialized with timezone information preserved (e.g., ISO format with timezone) or as naive datetime strings?
For Decimal, should the serialization be a string representation (as in str(obj)) or a numeric type (e.g., float) if possible?
Should numpy arrays of nested objects (e.g., arrays of arrays) be recursively serialized via tolist(), and does tolist() handle all numpy dtypes (e.g., complex, object) appropriately?
If an unsupported type is encountered, should the custom encoder attempt to call a .to_json() or similar method on the object before falling back to the default encoder?
Should the JSON output be formatted with any specific indentation or separators (e.g., compact vs pretty-printed)?
For datetime objects, if they are naive (no timezone), should they be serialized as ISO format without timezone or with a default UTC marker?
Should the custom encoder handle subclasses of the supported types (e.g., a custom Decimal subclass) automatically, or only exact types?

If a numpy array contains unsupported elements (e.g., datetime objects), should tolist() be called first, and then those elements processed by the custom encoder, or should the array be processed element-wise?
